finding.claim: The purge handler calls checkPerm(u, "admin") but discards the boolean result, so the admin check is never enforced. Any caller who reaches the handler can run purgeAll(). rotateKeys uses mustPerm correctly, which shows the intended pattern.
finding.source: Any authenticated (or otherwise routed) HTTP request to the purge endpoint, including a user without the admin permission.
finding.sink: purgeAll() at handlers.go:27, a destructive admin-only operation.

trace.note: u := userFrom(r) loads the requesting user from the request context
checkPerm(u, "admin") returns false for non-admins but the result is ignored, with no early return or error response

finding.guards_checked: Only one file exists, so no routing or middleware could be inspected; a middleware that enforces admin on this route is not visible in this directory. Within the handler there is no other guard. mustPerm (handlers.go:16-22) would have worked but is not used here. The type assertion in userFrom (handlers.go:40) is a separate issue (it panics if no user is set) and not an authorization bypass.

verdict.guard_found: none (checkPerm at handlers.go:12-14 returns a bool that is discarded at line 26; no middleware visible in this single-file directory)
verdict.reason: handlers.go:26 calls checkPerm(u, "admin") as a bare statement, discarding its bool (defined at handlers.go:12-14, which neither aborts nor writes an error), so purgeAll() at handlers.go:27 runs for any user who reaches the handler, unlike rotateKeys, which tests mustPerm at handlers.go:33.
